Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the draft order form — attaching the MSA redlines (MSA_Nova_redline_v1.docx) and a PDF with our inline comments on the order form. High level: we are OK with Redwood's standard service levels, but two open items from legal:

- Governing law & venue: we prefer Delaware but can consider CA if Redwood is firm about it and we can add reciprocal injunctive relief language.
- Interim equitable relief: Nova needs clear language that doesn’t preclude their ability to seek emergency injunctive relief (e.g., to protect customer data).
- Service of process / escrow: our procurement team wants an escrow contact and a service-of-process address in North America.

Can you confirm Redwood's stance on (1) law seat (Delaware vs. California) and (2) whether Redwood will accept an explicit carveout for injunctive relief (no waiver of emergency equitable relief) for data/privacy incidents?

We can jump on a quick call today if easier — copied Bryan from outside counsel for any legal nuance.

Thanks,
Samantha Greene
Head of Procurement, NovaCorp

Samantha —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. Quick summary of Redwood's positions (so legal and procurement are aligned on the call):

1) Governing law & forum: our standard is California (State of CA) for the MSA; for the order form we can be flexible to accept Delaware as long as we preserve: (a) Redwood's right to seek emergency provisional remedies in any competent court; and (b) mutual waiver language doesn't prevent expedited injunctive relief.

2) Interim equitable relief carveout: we will accept a carveout that explicitly preserves either party's right to seek emergency injunctive relief to protect intellectual property, trade secrets, or customer data. Redwood will not agree to language that requires exhaustion of remedies or advance notice as a precondition for emergency relief.

3) Service of process & escrow: we can provide a North America service-of-process address and will add an escrow contact block in the order form. We need to confirm the escrow vendor and scope (binary vs full repo) — is Nova expecting code escrow or configuration/content?

Next steps I propose:
- Kar thik and Olga from Legal join a 30-min call this afternoon to walk through the attached redline and agree final phrasing for the carveout and the forum selection compromise.
- I'll prepare a 1-pager (redline-summary-priyom.txt) showing exact language options (CA seat + carveout example / Delaware seat + alternate wording).

If that works, propose 3:00pm PT today. If not, send times.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

- On escrow: Nova only needs an escrow arrangement that would allow us to restore customer-critical functionality in the event of prolonged vendor failure. We're not asking for source code in perpetuity; a narrowly scoped configuration/recovery artifact is sufficient.
- On injunctive carveout: we need the language to be symmetric and include a short notice provision ("reasonable notice where practicable") — we understand Redwood's reluctance on advance notice as a hard precondition.

Team — thanks for the call earlier. Notes and action items below (captured quickly so Legal can draft):

Call notes:
- Agreed principle: Redwood keeps CA as preferred seat; Nova will accept CA if Redwood adds a clear mutual carveout for emergency equitable relief and a short notice clause "where practicable."
- If Nova insists on Delaware as the law seat, Redwood requires explicit preservation of provisional remedies (i.e., a clause allowing either party to seek emergency relief in a local court without waiving arbitration).
- Escrow: Redwood agrees to include a limited recovery escrow (configuration/restore artifacts). Scope and vendor TBD. Procurement to confirm minimal restore artifact list.

Proposed draft snippets for legal: (Olga / Priyom — please convert to redline)
1) Emergency relief carveout: "Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate disputes, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, protect confidential information, or prevent irreparable harm; such actions shall not constitute a waiver of the parties' right to arbitration."

2) Governing law / forum: "The Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of California. Subject to the emergency relief carveout above, the parties agree that all disputes shall be resolved by binding arbitration in San Francisco, CA under the rules of the American Arbitration Association (or similar)."

3) Service of process / escrow block: add a Party contact block for service in NA and an escrow section referencing the vendor and scope (TBD).

Action items:
- Olga: prepare redline with the three snippets above and include both CA-seat and Delaware-seat variants (ETA: EOD 6/29).
- Priyom: confirm escrow scope with Nova procurement (Samantha).
- Samantha / Bryan: confirm that the mutual carveout language above would be acceptable to Nova and their counsel; if yes, we can push final redline to procurement for signatures.

I'll track progress in HubSpot. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/9042/DEAL-9042
